questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Manjra is a tributary of the Godavari, along with the Pranhita, Wardha and Wainganga. The Tungabhadra, Bhima and Koyna are all tributaries of the Krishna. Memory hook: Godavari = Manjra, Pranhita; Krishna = Tungabhadra, Bhima, Koyna.

questions.question_text: Which river flows through the capital cities of Vienna, Budapest and Belgrade?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): The Rhine is the other great river of central Europe and flows through Basel and Cologne, so students pick it.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Danube flows through four capitals, namely Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade, before emptying into the Black Sea. Memory hook: Danube = River of capitals.

questions.question_text: Brass is an alloy of which two metals?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): Copper and tin is bronze, the other well-known copper alloy, so students swap the two.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Brass is made from copper and zinc and is used in utensils and musical instruments. Bronze is copper and tin, solder is lead and tin, and steel is iron with carbon. Memory hook: Brass = Copper + Zinc.

questions.question_text: Which instrument is used to measure the relative humidity of the air?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The hydrometer has a similar-sounding name but measures the density of liquids, not moisture in air.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: A hygrometer measures the amount of water vapour in the air. An anemometer measures wind speed and a barometer measures atmospheric pressure. Memory hook: Hygro = moisture.

questions.question_text: Which compound, used as a mild anaesthetic, is commonly known as 'laughing gas'?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Nitric oxide (NO) has a very similar name to nitrous oxide (N2O), so the two are swapped.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is called laughing gas and is used as a mild anaesthetic. Nitric oxide is NO and nitrogen dioxide is NO2, a brown toxic gas. Memory hook: Nitrous = N2O = Two nitrogens, laughing.

questions.question_text: Kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis) is caused by which organism?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Trypanosoma is a similar flagellated protozoan, but it causes sleeping sickness, so students swap the two.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Kala-azar is caused by the protozoan Leishmania donovani and spread by the bite of the sandfly. Entamoeba causes amoebic dysentery and Plasmodium causes malaria. Memory hook: Kala-azar = Sandfly + Leishmania.

questions.question_text: In which type of bank account does a depositor deposit a fixed sum every month for a fixed tenure and receive the maturity amount with interest at the end?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): A Fixed Deposit also pays interest at maturity, but it involves a single lump-sum deposit, so students confuse the two term deposits.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: A Recurring Deposit builds savings through regular monthly instalments over a fixed tenure. A Fixed Deposit is a one-time lump-sum deposit for a fixed term. Memory hook: RD = Regular instalments.

questions.question_text: In the money market, funds borrowed or lent for a period between 2 days and 14 days are called:
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Call money is the closest neighbour, but it covers borrowing for only one day, not 2 to 14 days.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Per the RBI, money borrowed or lent for one day is call money, for 2 to 14 days it is notice money, and for periods beyond 14 days it is term money. Memory hook: Call = 1 day, Notice = 2 to 14 days, Term = beyond 14.

questions.question_text: In national income accounting, which of the following is equal to 'National Income'?

options.A: Gross Domestic Product at market prices
options.B: Net National Product at factor cost
options.C: Net Domestic Product at market prices
options.D: Gross National Product at market prices

questions.trap_type: Trap (D): GNP at market prices is popularly called the national product, so students pick it, but it includes depreciation and indirect taxes.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Net National Product at factor cost equals GNP at market prices minus depreciation minus net indirect taxes, and this is the National Income. Memory hook: National Income = NNP at factor cost.

questions.question_text: Which Greek ambassador at the Mauryan court wrote the account 'Indica', describing life in the Mauryan empire?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Seleucus Nicator was the Greek ruler who sent the ambassador after his treaty with the Mauryas, so students pick the sender instead of the writer.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Megasthenes stayed at Pataliputra as the envoy of Seleucus I, and his Indica survives only in fragments quoted by later writers. Fa-Xian and Hiuen Tsang were Chinese pilgrims of much later periods. Memory hook: Megasthenes = Mauryan envoy = Indica.

questions.question_text: Construction of the Qutb Minar in Delhi was begun by Qutbuddin Aibak and completed by which Sultan?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): Alauddin Khalji added the Alai Darwaza and started the unfinished Alai Minar in the same complex, so students credit him with the Qutb Minar.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Aibak began the tower, and Iltutmish completed the upper storeys. Firoz Shah Tughlaq later repaired the top storeys after lightning damage. Memory hook: Aibak starts, Iltutmish finishes.

questions.question_text: Who led the Revolt of 1857 at Lucknow, proclaiming her young son Birjis Qadr as the Nawab of Awadh?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi is the best-known woman leader of 1857, so students pick her for every leadership question.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Begum Hazrat Mahal, wife of the deposed Nawab Wajid Ali Shah, took charge of the rebellion at Lucknow. Nana Saheb led at Kanpur and Kunwar Singh at Jagdishpur in Bihar. Memory hook: Lucknow = Hazrat Mahal, Kanpur = Nana Saheb.

questions.question_text: The All India Congress Committee adopted the Quit India resolution on 8 August 1942 at which place?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The Congress Working Committee passed the preliminary resolution at Wardha in July 1942, so students pick Wardha for the final adoption.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The AICC session at Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay adopted the resolution, and Gandhi gave the call 'Do or Die' there. The ground is now known as August Kranti Maidan. Memory hook: Wardha drafts, Gowalia Tank adopts.

questions.question_text: The Shore Temple at Mamallapuram, a structural temple built of cut stone, was constructed during the reign of which Pallava ruler?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) gave Mamallapuram its name and is linked with its rock-cut monuments, so students credit him with the Shore Temple.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Shore Temple dates to the early eighth century and belongs to Narasimhavarman II, also called Rajasimha. Unlike the earlier rock-cut caves and rathas, it is a free-standing structural temple. Memory hook: Mamalla = rock-cut, Rajasimha = structural shore temple.

questions.question_text: Sattriya, recognised as a classical dance form by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000, originated in the monasteries (Sattras) of which state?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Manipur has its own classical dance, Manipuri, which is another north-eastern form, so students pick it.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Sattriya was developed in the fifteenth century by Srimanta Sankardeva as part of the Vaishnava Sattras of Assam. It was added to the list of classical dances in 2000. Memory hook: Sattriya = Sattra = Assam.

questions.question_text: The Sundarbans National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its mangrove forests, is located in which Indian state?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Bhitarkanika in Odisha is another famous mangrove area, so students pick Odisha.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Indian Sundarbans lie in the delta of the Ganga and Brahmaputra in West Bengal and were inscribed on the World Heritage List in 1987. The mangroves are home to the Royal Bengal tiger. Memory hook: Sundarbans = Sundari trees = Bengal delta.

questions.question_text: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is a renowned maestro of which musical instrument?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Santoor is another Hindustani instrument, linked with Pandit Shivkumar Sharma, so students swap the two maestros.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Hariprasad Chaurasia is a leading exponent of the bansuri, the bamboo flute of Hindustani classical music. Sarod is associated with Ustad Amjad Ali Khan. Memory hook: Chaurasia = Bansuri.

questions.question_text: The headquarters of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), a specialised agency of the United Nations, is located in which city?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): Geneva hosts many UN agencies, so students make it the default guess for any specialised agency.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: ICAO was created under the Chicago Convention of 1944 and is headquartered in Montreal, Canada. The International Maritime Organization is in London and the Food and Agriculture Organization is in Rome. Memory hook: ICAO = Air = Montreal.

questions.question_text: The term 'Gambit' is used in which game?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): Bridge is another mind sport with its own jargon such as trump, rubber and slam, so students pick it.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: A gambit is an opening in chess in which a pawn or piece is sacrificed to gain an advantage in position, as in the Queen's Gambit. Memory hook: Gambit = Gamble in chess.

questions.question_text: Part IX-A of the Constitution of India, containing Articles 243P to 243ZG, deals with which of the following?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Part IX deals with Panchayats and sits right before Part IX-A, so students pick the neighbouring Part.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Part IX-A covers Municipalities, which are urban local bodies. Part IX-B on Co-operative Societies was added later by the 97th Amendment, and Part XIV-A deals with Tribunals. Memory hook: IX = village, IX-A = city.

questions.question_text: Who administers the oath of office to the President of India?

options.A: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha

questions.trap_type: Trap (D): The Vice-President is the second-highest officer and acts as President in a vacancy, so students pick him.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 60 says the oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India or, in his absence, the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court available. Memory hook: Article 60 = oath by the CJI.

questions.question_text: The Right to Property was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights and made a constitutional right under Article 300A by which Amendment?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): The 25th Amendment curtailed the right to property by changing Article 31, so it is the closest confusion with the amendment that finally removed it.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The 44th Amendment omitted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 and inserted Article 300A in Part XII, so property is now a legal right and not a Fundamental Right. Memory hook: 44th = property out, 300A = property in as a legal right.

questions.question_text: Which Article of the Constitution prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour (begar)?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Article 24 prohibits child labour in factories and mines and sits right after Article 23, so students pick the adjacent Article.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Articles 23 and 24 together form the Right against Exploitation. Article 17 abolishes untouchability and Article 25 gives freedom of religion. Memory hook: 23 = Adults exploited, 24 = Children exploited.

questions.question_text: The Toda, a pastoral community known for its barrel-vaulted huts, lives mainly in the Nilgiri hills of which state?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Kerala also borders the Nilgiris and has many tribal groups, so students pick the neighbouring state.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Todas are concentrated in the Nilgiri district of Tamil Nadu and are traditionally buffalo herders. Memory hook: Toda = Nilgiri = Tamil Nadu.

questions.question_text: The Malanjkhand copper mines, in the Balaghat district, are located in which state?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): Rajasthan's Khetri belt is the most famous copper-mining area, so students pick Rajasthan.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Balaghat mines of Madhya Pradesh, which include Malanjkhand, are the leading source of copper in India. Singhbhum in Jharkhand and Khetri in Rajasthan are the other major belts. Memory hook: Balaghat = Madhya Pradesh copper.

questions.question_text: Sambhar Lake, the largest inland saltwater lake of India, is located in which state?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The Rann of Kutch in Gujarat is a salty region and a major salt producer, so students pick Gujarat.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Sambhar Lake lies near Jaipur and is a major source of salt. It is also a recognised Ramsar wetland. Memory hook: Sambhar = Salt = Rajasthan.

questions.question_text: The Namib Desert, a coastal desert along the Atlantic Ocean, lies mainly in which country?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): The Kalahari Desert spreads across Botswana and lies next to the Namib, so students pick Botswana.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Namib runs along the coast of Namibia, and the country takes its name from the desert. The Kalahari lies inland to the east, covering Botswana and parts of neighbouring countries. Memory hook: Namib = Namibia.

questions.question_text: Which is the hardest naturally occurring substance?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Graphite is also an allotrope of carbon, so students confuse it with diamond, but it is soft and slippery.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: In diamond each carbon atom is bonded to four others in a rigid three-dimensional network, which makes it the hardest natural substance. Graphite has layers that slide over each other. Memory hook: Diamond = Dense network = Hardest.

questions.question_text: Which scientist discovered the neutron in 1932?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Rutherford discovered the atomic nucleus and the proton and guided Chadwick, so students credit him with the neutron.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: James Chadwick discovered the neutron, a particle with no charge and mass about equal to a proton. Thomson discovered the electron and Bohr proposed the orbit model. Memory hook: Chadwick = Chargeless neutron.

questions.question_text: In the human nephron, most of the selective reabsorption of glucose and amino acids from the filtrate takes place in the:
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The Loop of Henle is the best-known region for water reabsorption and concentrating urine, so students pick it.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The proximal convoluted tubule reabsorbs nearly all essential nutrients such as glucose and amino acids, along with much of the water and electrolytes. The Loop of Henle and collecting duct mainly regulate water and urine concentration. Memory hook: Proximal = Primary reabsorption.

questions.question_text: IMPS (Immediate Payment Service), which allows instant interbank fund transfers through mobile and internet round the clock, is operated by which organisation?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): The RBI regulates payment systems and itself operates NEFT and RTGS, so students assume it also runs IMPS.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: NPCI is the umbrella organisation for retail payments in India, set up in 2008 with the guidance of the RBI and the Indian Banks' Association. It operates IMPS, UPI and RuPay. Memory hook: NPCI = Retail payments, RBI = Regulator and NEFT/RTGS.

questions.question_text: Which type of bank account, mostly opened by traders and businesses, normally pays no interest and has no limit on the number of transactions?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The savings account is the most common account, but it pays interest and has limits on transactions, so students confuse the two demand accounts.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: A current account is meant for frequent business transactions and usually pays no interest. A Demat account holds securities in electronic form and is not a deposit account. Memory hook: Current account = Constant business flow.

questions.question_text: Treasury Bills issued by the Government of India are currently issued in which three maturities?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): 365 days sounds like a natural one-year bill, but the longest Treasury Bill matures in 364 days.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Treasury Bills are zero-coupon money market instruments issued at a discount and redeemed at face value. The three tenors are 91, 182 and 364 days. Memory hook: 91, 182, 364 = 13, 26, 52 weeks.

questions.question_text: Which Five Year Plan, launched in 1992 after the economic reforms of 1991, placed human development, including employment, education and public health, at the centre of its objectives?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): The Ninth Plan stressed growth with social justice and equity, a similar social theme, so students pick it.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Eighth Plan (1992 to 1997) began after the reforms of 1991 and made human development its main focus, along with modernisation and growth. Memory hook: Eighth = Human development after reforms.

questions.question_text: The Buddhist Council held at Pataliputra during the reign of Emperor Ashoka, under the presidency of Moggaliputta Tissa, was the:
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The Second Council was held at Vaishali about a century after the Buddha's death, and students confuse the two because both dealt with disputes over monastic discipline.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Third Council at Pataliputra, held under Ashoka, aimed to purify the Sangha and settle doctrinal disputes. The Fourth Council was held in Kashmir under Kanishka. Memory hook: Third = Ashoka = Pataliputra.

questions.question_text: Gautamiputra Satakarni, the most celebrated Satavahana ruler, is credited with defeating and destroying the power of which Western Kshatrapa ruler, whose coins he restruck?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Rudradaman I is the best-known Kshatrapa ruler and fought the Satavahanas, but he belonged to a later generation and defeated a Satavahana successor, not Gautamiputra.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated Nahapana of the Kshaharata line, and a hoard of Nahapana's silver coins restruck with Satavahana marks was found near Nashik. Rudradaman I of the Ujjain line came later. Memory hook: Gautamiputra beats Nahapana, Rudradaman comes after.

questions.question_text: Shivaji was crowned Chhatrapati in 1674 at which fort, which he also made his capital?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): Rajgad was Shivaji's earlier seat of government before he shifted to Raigad, so students pick it as the capital.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Shivaji's formal coronation took place at Raigad, which became the capital of the Maratha kingdom. Pratapgad is remembered for the encounter with Afzal Khan and Sinhagad for the capture of Kondana. Memory hook: Raigad = Royal coronation.

questions.question_text: The Satyashodhak Samaj, founded in 1873 to secure social justice for the lower castes, was established by:
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): Dayananda Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj only two years later, in 1875, so the two reform bodies of the 1870s get swapped.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Jyotirao Phule set up the Satyashodhak Samaj in Pune and attacked caste hierarchy and Brahmanical dominance, writing Gulamgiri in 1873. Memory hook: Phule = Pune = Satyashodhak.

questions.question_text: The Indian National Congress split into the Moderate and Extremist camps at its Surat session in 1907. Who presided over this session?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): The Extremist camp had wanted Lajpat Rai as president, which is exactly the dispute behind the split, so students assume he presided.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Rash Behari Ghosh, the Moderates' choice, presided at Surat, and the session broke up amid disorder. The split lasted until the Lucknow Congress of 1916. Memory hook: Surat 1907 = Ghosh, split.

questions.question_text: Madhubani painting, a folk art tradition known for its intricate line work and vivid natural colours, originated in the Mithila region of which state?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Warli painting from Maharashtra is the other famous tribal folk art, so the two are often swapped.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Madhubani, also called Mithila painting, comes from the Mithila region of Bihar and traditionally decorated walls and floors of homes. Memory hook: Madhubani = Mithila = Bihar.

questions.question_text: The famous group of temples at Khajuraho in Madhya Pradesh, known for its Nagara-style architecture and sculpture, was built by which dynasty?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The Rashtrakutas built the monolithic Kailasa temple at Ellora, another famous sculpted temple, so the dynasties get mixed up.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Chandela rulers of Bundelkhand built the Khajuraho temples roughly between 950 and 1050 CE. The Hoysalas are known for the temples at Belur and Halebidu. Memory hook: Chandela = Khajuraho.

questions.question_text: The Tehri Dam, a major multipurpose project in Uttarakhand, is built on which river?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): The Alaknanda is the other headstream that joins the Bhagirathi at Devprayag to form the Ganga, so it is the closest confusion.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Tehri Dam stands on the Bhagirathi near its confluence with the Bhilangana in Tehri Garhwal district. It serves irrigation, drinking water and hydropower. Memory hook: Tehri = Bhagirathi.

questions.question_text: The Gateway of India in Mumbai was built to commemorate the 1911 landing in India of which British monarch?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Queen Victoria was Empress of India and many colonial monuments honour her, so students attach this one to her too.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: King George V and Queen Mary landed at Apollo Bunder in December 1911, and the arch designed by George Wittet was built to mark the visit and completed in 1924. Memory hook: Gateway = George V.

questions.question_text: Which was the first Biosphere Reserve to be established in India, in 1986?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Nanda Devi was notified only two years later, in 1988, and is the best-known Himalayan reserve, so students pick it.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, spread across Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka, was India's first, in 1986. Gulf of Mannar followed in 1989 and Pachmarhi in 1999. Memory hook: Nilgiri = Number one.

questions.question_text: Which of the following subjects is included in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Central police forces exist, so students assume police is a Union subject, but it is a State List subject.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Defence of India is Entry 1 of the Union List. Police, agriculture and public health are State List subjects. Memory hook: Defence = Delhi decides.

questions.question_text: Which of the following sentences can be pardoned by the President under Article 72 but is outside the pardoning power of the Governor under Article 161?

options.A: A sentence passed by a court martial
options.B: A sentence for which a reprieve, respite or remission is sought
options.C: A sentence for an offence under a State law
options.D: A sentence that is to be suspended

questions.trap_type: Trap (C): The Governor's power extends to offences against State laws, so students think it is the area that belongs only to the President.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 72 gives the President power over sentences by court martial and over offences under Union law, while Article 161 limits the Governor to matters in the State's executive power. Both can grant reprieves, respites, remissions and suspensions. Memory hook: Court martial = President only.

questions.question_text: Which writ is issued by a higher court to stop a lower court or tribunal from continuing proceedings in a case that is beyond its jurisdiction?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Certiorari also deals with lower courts exceeding jurisdiction, but it quashes an order already passed, while Prohibition acts while proceedings are pending.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Prohibition is a preventive writ issued while the case is pending, whereas Certiorari is corrective and issued after the order. Both are available under Articles 32 and 226. Memory hook: Prohibition = Prevent, Certiorari = Cancel.

questions.question_text: A member of a State Public Service Commission holds office for six years or until attaining which age, whichever is earlier?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): 65 years is the age limit for a member of the UPSC, so the two limits are swapped.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 316(2) fixes six years or the age of 62 for State Public Service Commission members, and six years or the age of 65 for the UPSC. Memory hook: Union = 65, State = 62.

questions.question_text: The strong, gusty, hot and dry wind that blows during summer afternoons over the northern and north-western plains of India is called:
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Kalbaisakhi is also a summer phenomenon, but it is a thunderstorm of Bengal and not a hot dry wind.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Loo is a hot and dry wind of the northern plains in May and June. Mango showers occur in Kerala and Karnataka, and Kalbaisakhi in West Bengal. Memory hook: Loo = Lethal heat in the plains.

questions.question_text: Which cold ocean current flows along the western coast of South America?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The Benguela Current is the matching cold current off the western coast of southern Africa, so the two continents get swapped.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Peru or Humboldt Current is a cold current in the south-eastern Pacific along the coast of Peru and Chile. Brazil Current is warm and Kuroshio is a warm current in the north-western Pacific. Memory hook: Peru = Pacific = Cold.

questions.question_text: Which Indian port is described as the deepest landlocked and well-protected port?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Paradip is known as a deep-sea harbour handling iron ore exports, so students link 'deep' with Paradip.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Visakhapatnam on the east coast is the deepest landlocked and well-protected port. Chennai is an artificial harbour and Tuticorin is a major port in Tamil Nadu. Memory hook: Vizag = Very deep and sheltered.

questions.question_text: The hill station of Kodaikanal in Tamil Nadu lies in which hill range?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The Nilgiris hold Udhagamandalam (Ooty), the best-known Tamil Nadu hill station, so students place Kodaikanal there too.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Kodaikanal is in the Palani Hills, an eastward spur of the Western Ghats in Dindigul district. Ooty is in the Nilgiris. Memory hook: Kodaikanal = Palani.

questions.question_text: The financial year of the Government of India runs from:
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): The calendar year is the everyday year, so students assume the financial year follows it.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The General Clauses Act, 1897 defines the financial year as the year commencing on 1 April, and the Union Budget covers this period. Memory hook: April to March.

questions.question_text: As per RBI norms, a loan is classified as a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) when interest or principal remains overdue for more than how many days?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): 60 days falls within the 'special mention' stage (SMA-1 is 31 to 60 days overdue), so students mistake an early-warning stage for an NPA.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: An asset becomes an NPA when interest or instalment is overdue for more than 90 days. 180 days was an older norm that was tightened to 90 days. Memory hook: 90 days overdue = NPA.

questions.question_text: As per RBI's Basel III guidelines, the minimum total capital to risk-weighted assets ratio (CRAR) for Indian scheduled commercial banks, excluding the capital conservation buffer, is:
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): 8 percent is the minimum prescribed by the Basel Committee itself, while RBI has set a stricter 9 percent for Indian banks.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: RBI requires banks to maintain a minimum total capital of 9 percent of risk-weighted assets, which rises to 11.5 percent after adding the 2.5 percent capital conservation buffer. Memory hook: Basel says 8, RBI says 9.

questions.question_text: Fiscal deficit in the Government Budget is equal to total expenditure minus:

options.C: Revenue receipts plus non-debt capital receipts

questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Subtracting only revenue receipts ignores non-debt capital receipts such as recovery of loans and disinvestment, so the deficit comes out too large.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Fiscal deficit equals total expenditure minus total receipts excluding borrowings, and the gap is the amount the government must borrow. Including borrowings in receipts would make the deficit zero by definition. Memory hook: Fiscal deficit = Borrowing requirement.

questions.question_text: Phenolphthalein indicator turns which colour in a basic solution?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): Methyl orange turns yellow in basic solution, so the two indicators get mixed up.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic and neutral solutions and turns pink in bases. Methyl orange is red in acid and yellow in base. Memory hook: Phenolphthalein = Pink in base.

questions.question_text: Taking the speed of sound in air as 344 m/s at 22 degrees Celsius, what is the minimum distance of a reflecting surface from the source needed to hear a distinct echo?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): 34.4 m is the total distance covered by sound in 0.1 second, and students forget that the sound travels to the obstacle and back, so the one-way distance is half.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The ear retains a sound for about 0.1 s, so the echo must arrive after that gap. Total path = 344 x 0.1 = 34.4 m, and the one-way distance = 34.4 / 2 = 17.2 m. Memory hook: Echo needs 17.2 m, halve the round trip.

questions.question_text: Which plant hormone is commonly called the 'stress hormone' because it helps plants cope with conditions such as water shortage by closing stomata?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): Auxin is the best-known plant hormone, so students choose it for any hormone question.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Abscisic acid inhibits growth, promotes closing of stomata and helps plants withstand stress. Cytokinins promote cell division and gibberellins promote stem elongation. Memory hook: ABA = Alarm hormone.

questions.question_text: Who was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): Parshvanatha was the 23rd Tirthankara, immediately before Mahavira, so students pick him as the nearest earlier teacher.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Vardhamana Mahavira, born in the sixth century BCE near Vaishali, was the 24th and last Tirthankara of the Jains. Rishabhanatha was the first Tirthankara. Memory hook: Mahavira = 24th = Last.

questions.question_text: Which Pallava ruler wrote the Sanskrit farce 'Mattavilasa Prahasana'?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla) was Mahendravarman's son and the better-known Pallava king, so students credit him with the work.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Mahendravarman I, who ruled in the early seventh century CE, composed Mattavilasa Prahasana, a satirical Sanskrit one-act play. He is also known for patronising rock-cut cave temples. Memory hook: Mahendravarman = Mattavilasa (both start with M).

questions.question_text: Which Viceroy is regarded as the 'Father of Local Self-Government' in India because of his resolution of 1882 on local bodies?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Lord Mayo's 1870 resolution on financial decentralisation was an earlier step towards local finance, so students credit him with the 1882 reform.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882 encouraged elected non-official majorities in local boards and gave them real powers. Mayo's 1870 resolution only devolved certain finances to the provinces. Memory hook: Ripon = Rural and urban local bodies.

questions.question_text: Separate electorates for Muslims were first introduced in British India by which Act?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): The 1919 Act extended separate electorates to Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans, so students think it introduced them.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Indian Councils Act, 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) provided separate electorates for Muslims for the first time. Later Acts extended the principle to other communities. Memory hook: 1909 = Minto = Muslim electorates.

questions.question_text: Which Act redesignated the Governor-General of Bengal as the Governor-General of India and ended the East India Company's role as a commercial body?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): The Charter Act of 1813 ended the Company's trade monopoly except in tea and the China trade, so students pick it for the end of the commercial role.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Charter Act of 1833 made Lord William Bentinck the first Governor-General of India and turned the Company into a purely administrative body. The Charter Act of 1853 later added non-official members to the legislative council and opened up the civil service to competition. Memory hook: 1833 = One India, one Governor-General.

questions.question_text: The Pamban Bridge, India's first sea bridge, connects the mainland with which island?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Sriharikota is also an island on the south-eastern coast, so students pick it by region.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The Pamban Bridge, opened in 1914, links the mainland of Tamil Nadu with Rameswaram (Pamban) Island across the Palk Strait. Elephanta is near Mumbai and Majuli is a river island in the Brahmaputra. Memory hook: Pamban = Pilgrims to Rameswaram.

questions.question_text: In Dravidian temple architecture, the monumental gateway tower at the entrance of the temple complex is called the:
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): The Vimana is also a tall tower in Dravidian temples, but it stands over the sanctum and not over the entrance.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: A gopuram is the large, ornate gateway tower of South Indian temples and became taller in later periods such as Chola and Vijayanagara times. The Shikhara is the tower of Nagara temples. Memory hook: Gopuram = Gate.

questions.question_text: Phad, a long cloth scroll painting that narrates the epics of folk heroes such as Pabuji and Devnarayan, belongs to which region?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Odisha's Pattachitra is also a cloth-based narrative painting, so students link the two scroll traditions.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Phad paintings are made by the Joshi community of Bhilwara and Shahpura in Rajasthan and are shown during storytelling performances by Bhopa priest-singers. Cheriyal scrolls come from Telangana and Patua scrolls from Bengal. Memory hook: Phad = Pabuji = Rajasthan.

questions.question_text: India's premier first-class cricket championship, the Ranji Trophy, is named after:
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Duleepsinhji was Ranjitsinhji's nephew and has the Duleep Trophy named after him, so the two trophies get swapped.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The trophy honours Ranjitsinhji, the Jam Sahib of Nawanagar, who played Test cricket for England. The Duleep Trophy is the zonal tournament named after Duleepsinhji. Memory hook: Ranji Trophy = Ranjitsinhji.

questions.question_text: The Keibul Lamjao National Park, known for its floating phumdis and the endangered sangai deer, lies on which lake?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): Dal Lake is famous for its floating gardens, so students link it with 'floating' vegetation.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Keibul Lamjao in Manipur is the world's only floating national park and sits on the southern part of Loktak Lake. The floating mats of vegetation, soil and organic matter are called phumdis. Memory hook: Loktak = Manipur = Sangai.

questions.question_text: Which writ is issued to secure the release of a person who has been illegally detained?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Mandamus is the best-known writ and means 'we command', so students pick it for any case where a court gives an order.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Habeas Corpus means 'you may have the body' and requires the detaining authority to produce the person before the court. Quo Warranto questions the legal authority of a person holding a public office. Memory hook: Habeas = Have the body.

questions.question_text: Under which Article can Parliament create a new All-India Service common to the Union and the States if the Rajya Sabha declares by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting that it is necessary in the national interest?
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): Article 311 protects civil servants from dismissal without inquiry and is the best-known Article in the same Part, so students pick it.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 312 allows Parliament to legislate for new All-India Services once the Rajya Sabha passes such a resolution. Article 310 deals with the tenure of civil servants at the pleasure of the President or Governor, and Article 313 with transitional provisions. Memory hook: 312 = Create All-India Services.

questions.question_text: The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office only in the same manner and on the same grounds as a:
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President, so students assume constitutional officers are removed in the same loose manner.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The proviso to Article 324(5) protects the Chief Election Commissioner's independence by giving him the same removal procedure as a Supreme Court judge, which is impeachment by Parliament. Other Election Commissioners can be removed only on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner. Memory hook: CEC removal = like a Supreme Court judge.

questions.question_text: How can the Vice-President of India be removed from office before the end of the five-year term?

options.A: By impeachment by two-thirds of the total membership of each House
options.B: By a resolution passed by two-thirds of the members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha alone
options.C: By a resolution passed by a simple majority in a joint sitting of both Houses
options.D: By a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Rajya Sabha and agreed to by the Lok Sabha

questions.trap_type: Trap (A): This is the impeachment procedure for the President under Article 61, so students apply it to the Vice-President.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Article 67(b) provides that the Vice-President can be removed by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of all its then members and agreed to by the Lok Sabha, after at least fourteen days' notice. No special majority and no joint sitting is needed. Memory hook: President = Impeachment, Vice-President = Resolution.

questions.question_text: Which winds bring most of the annual rainfall to the Tamil Nadu coast during October to December?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): The south-west monsoon gives most of India its rainfall, but Tamil Nadu lies in its rain shadow, so students pick it by default.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: During the retreating monsoon, north-east winds pick up moisture from the Bay of Bengal and cause rain on the Tamil Nadu and southern Andhra coasts. Western disturbances bring winter rain to north-west India. Memory hook: Oct to Dec, Tamil Nadu = North-east monsoon.

questions.question_text: Which lake is the deepest in the world, with a maximum depth of over 1,600 metres?
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Lake Tanganyika is the second deepest lake and the longest freshwater lake, so students pick it as the deepest.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Lake Baikal in Siberia, Russia, is the deepest lake in the world and holds a very large share of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water. Lake Superior is the largest freshwater lake by area and Victoria is Africa's largest lake by area. Memory hook: Baikal = Bottomless.

questions.question_text: Which tidal port in Kachchh, Gujarat, was developed soon after Independence to ease the pressure on Mumbai port after the loss of Karachi port?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Nhava Sheva (Jawaharlal Nehru Port) was also built to decongest Mumbai port, but much later, in the 1980s, and is in Maharashtra.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Kandla was the first major port developed after Partition, when Karachi went to Pakistan, and it handles large volumes of grain, salt and fertiliser. Mormugao is in Goa and Tuticorin in Tamil Nadu. Memory hook: Kandla = Kachchh = Karachi's replacement.

questions.question_text: In Bangladesh, the main channel of the Brahmaputra is known as the:
questions.trap_type: Trap (A): The Padma is the main channel of the Ganga in Bangladesh, which the Brahmaputra (Jamuna) joins, so students swap the two names.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: After entering Bangladesh, the Brahmaputra flows south as the Jamuna and meets the Padma, the Ganga's channel. Their combined stream later joins the Meghna and falls into the Bay of Bengal. Dihang or Siang is its name in Arunachal Pradesh. Memory hook: Brahmaputra = Dihang in India, Jamuna in Bangladesh.

questions.question_text: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) requirement for banks is prescribed under which provision?

options.A: Section 42 of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
options.B: Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
options.C: Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
options.D: Section 22 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949

questions.trap_type: Trap (A): Section 42 of the RBI Act is the provision for the Cash Reserve Ratio, the other reserve requirement, so students swap the two.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 requires banks to maintain a percentage of their demand and time liabilities in liquid assets such as cash, gold and approved securities. Section 35A gives the RBI power to issue directions to banks and Section 22 deals with licensing. Memory hook: SLR = Section 24, BR Act.

questions.question_text: Revenue deficit in the Union Budget is the excess of:

options.C: Total expenditure over total receipts excluding borrowings

questions.trap_type: Trap (C): This is the definition of fiscal deficit, the best-known budget deficit, so students use it for revenue deficit.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Revenue deficit means the government's day-to-day spending exceeds its revenue (tax and non-tax) receipts, which implies borrowing even for consumption. Fiscal deficit minus interest payments is the primary deficit. Memory hook: Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure minus Revenue receipts.

questions.question_text: Which money market instrument is an unsecured short-term promissory note issued mainly by highly rated corporates to raise funds?
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): A Certificate of Deposit is also an unsecured short-term money market instrument, but it is issued by banks and not by corporates.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Commercial Paper lets companies with a good credit rating borrow directly from investors for short periods. Treasury Bills are issued by the Government and call money is inter-bank borrowing for one day. Memory hook: CP = Corporate Paper, CD = Customer Deposit at a bank.

questions.question_text: A person who can see nearby objects clearly but cannot see distant objects clearly (myopia) is corrected using which lens?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): A convex lens corrects hypermetropia (far-sightedness), the opposite defect, so students swap the two.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: In myopia the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina. A concave lens of suitable power diverges the rays so the image forms on the retina. Memory hook: Myopia = Minus power = Concave.

questions.question_text: The painful burning sensation caused by a red ant's sting is mainly due to which acid?
questions.trap_type: Trap (D): Acetic acid is the familiar kitchen acid of vinegar, so students pick it as the most common weak acid.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Red ants inject formic acid (methanoic acid), and rubbing a mild base such as baking soda on the sting neutralises it and gives relief. The name formic comes from the Latin word for ant. Memory hook: Formic = Formica = Ant.

questions.question_text: In the chloroplast, the light-independent (dark) reactions of photosynthesis take place in the:
questions.trap_type: Trap (B): The grana are the stacks of thylakoids where the light reactions occur, so students place all of photosynthesis there.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: The light reactions occur in the thylakoid membranes of the grana, producing ATP and NADPH. These are used in the stroma, the fluid matrix, where the Calvin cycle fixes carbon dioxide into sugars. Memory hook: Grana = Light, Stroma = Sugar.

questions.question_text: The ABO blood group system was discovered by:
questions.trap_type: Trap (C): William Harvey is the famous scientist who described the circulation of blood, so students link every blood-related discovery to him.
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Karl Landsteiner identified the A, B and O blood groups, which made safe blood transfusion possible, and received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1930. Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine and Pasteur worked on germ theory and vaccines. Memory hook: Landsteiner = Labelled the blood groups.

questions.question_text: The price of a gadget is first raised by 20%, then reduced by 25%, and finally raised by 10%. What is the net change in its price compared with the original price?
questions.trap_type: Adding successive percentages
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Take the original price as 100. After +20% it is 120. Step 2: After -25% it is 120 x 0.75 = 90. Step 3: After +10% it is 90 x 1.10 = 99. Net change = 99 - 100 = 1% decrease. Shortcut: multiply the factors 1.20 x 0.75 x 1.10 = 0.99, so the price falls by 1%. Trap (D): Adding the percentages directly gives 20 - 25 + 10 = +5%, which is a 5% increase. Trap (C): Stopping after two steps gives 1.20 x 0.75 = 0.90, which is a 10% decrease, because the last 10% rise was forgotten. Trap (A): Treating the 25% decrease as an increase gives 1.20 x 1.25 x 1.10 = 1.65, which is a 65% increase.

questions.question_text: Vessel A contains a milk and water mixture in the ratio 3 : 2 and vessel B contains it in the ratio 1 : 4. In what ratio (A : B) should the two mixtures be mixed to get a mixture with milk and water in the ratio 1 : 1?
questions.trap_type: Alligating on the wrong quantity (inverted or ratio-as-concentration)
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Convert each mixture to the fraction of milk. A has 3/5 milk, B has 1/5 milk, and the target has 1/2 milk. Step 2: Use alligation. Quantity of A : Quantity of B = (target - B) : (A - target) = (1/2 - 1/5) : (3/5 - 1/2) = 3/10 : 1/10 = 3 : 1. Shortcut: milk fractions in tenths are A = 6, B = 2, mean = 5, so A : B = (5 - 2) : (6 - 5) = 3 : 1. Trap (A): Writing the differences the other way round gives 1 : 3, which is the inverted ratio. Trap (B): Alligating the milk-to-water ratios 3/2, 1/4 and 1 as if they were concentrations gives (1 - 1/4) : (3/2 - 1) = 3/4 : 1/2 = 3 : 2. Trap (C): Assuming equal quantities because the target ratio is 1 : 1 gives 1 : 1, but equal mixing gives only 2/5 milk, not 1/2.

questions.question_text: A invests Rs 36,000 for the full year. B invests Rs 48,000 and joins 3 months later. C invests Rs 24,000 and joins 6 months after the start. If the yearly profit is Rs 1,26,000, what is B's share?
questions.trap_type: Ignoring investment time or using joining time as duration
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Find capital x months. A = 36,000 x 12 = 4,32,000. B stays 12 - 3 = 9 months, so B = 48,000 x 9 = 4,32,000. C stays 12 - 6 = 6 months, so C = 24,000 x 6 = 1,44,000. Step 2: Ratio = 432 : 432 : 144 = 3 : 3 : 1. Step 3: B's share = 3/7 x 1,26,000 = Rs 54,000. Shortcut: reduce the ratio to 3 : 3 : 1 and divide 1,26,000 by 7 to get 18,000 per part. Trap (B): Ignoring time and using only capital gives 36 : 48 : 24 = 3 : 4 : 2, so B gets 4/9 x 1,26,000 = Rs 56,000. Trap (C): Using B's joining delay (3 months) as his duration gives 432 : 144 : 144 = 3 : 1 : 1, so B gets 1/5 x 1,26,000 = Rs 25,200. Trap (D): Splitting equally among three partners gives 1,26,000 / 3 = Rs 42,000.

questions.question_text: What is the compound interest on Rs 10,000 for 1.5 years at 20% per annum, compounded half-yearly?
questions.trap_type: Confusing simple interest or amount with compound interest
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Half-yearly compounding means the rate per period is 20/2 = 10% and the number of periods is 1.5 x 2 = 3. Step 2: Amount = 10,000 x 1.1 x 1.1 x 1.1 = 13,310. Step 3: Compound interest = 13,310 - 10,000 = Rs 3,310. Shortcut: three successive 10% rises give 10% + 10% + 10% + 1% + 1% + 1% + 0.1% = 33.1%, which is Rs 3,310 on 10,000. Trap (C): Using simple interest gives 10,000 x 20 x 1.5 / 100 = Rs 3,000. Trap (B): Giving the amount instead of the interest gives Rs 13,310. Trap (A): Not halving the rate but still using 3 periods gives 10,000 x (1.2 x 1.2 x 1.2 - 1) = 10,000 x 0.728 = Rs 7,280.

questions.concept_tag: Pipes and cistern with a leak
questions.question_text: Pipes A and B can fill an empty tank in 12 hours and 18 hours respectively, while a leak C can empty a full tank in 36 hours. If all three work together, in how many hours will the tank become 2/3 full?
questions.trap_type: Treating the leak as an inlet, ignoring it, or ignoring the fraction
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Take the tank as 36 units. A fills 3 units per hour, B fills 2 units per hour, and C empties 1 unit per hour. Net rate = 3 + 2 - 1 = 4 units per hour. Step 2: Full tank takes 36/4 = 9 hours. Step 3: For 2/3 of the tank, time = 2/3 x 9 = 6 hours. Shortcut: net work per hour is 1/9 of the tank, so 2/3 of the tank needs (2/3) x 9 = 6 hours. Trap (C): Forgetting the 2/3 fraction gives the time for a full tank, which is 9 hours. Trap (B): Treating the leak as another inlet gives a rate of 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 units per hour, so full time is 6 hours and 2/3 of it is 4 hours. Trap (A): Ignoring the leak gives a rate of 3 + 2 = 5 units per hour, so full time is 36/5 = 7.2 hours and 2/3 of it is 4.8 hours.

questions.question_text: The average weight of 7 workers is 62 kg. When one worker weighing 70 kg is replaced by a new worker, the average weight falls by 3 kg. What is the weight of the new worker?
questions.trap_type: Forgetting to multiply the change in average by the number of items
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: The average falls by 3 kg across 7 workers, so the total weight falls by 7 x 3 = 21 kg. Step 2: The new worker weighs 21 kg less than the worker who left, so new weight = 70 - 21 = 49 kg. Shortcut: new weight = old weight - (number of workers x fall in average) = 70 - 7 x 3 = 49. Trap (B): Taking the new average (62 - 3 = 59) as the new worker's weight gives 59 kg. Trap (D): Subtracting only the fall in average from 70 and not multiplying by 7 gives 70 - 3 = 67 kg. Trap (A): Adding instead of subtracting the total change gives 70 + 21 = 91 kg.

questions.question_text: A solid metal cylinder of diameter 12 cm and height 8 cm is melted and recast into solid spheres of radius 2 cm each. How many such spheres can be made?
questions.trap_type: Using a wrong volume formula or diameter as radius
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Cylinder radius = 12/2 = 6 cm. Volume = pi x 6 x 6 x 8 = 288 pi cm cube. Step 2: Sphere volume = (4/3) x pi x 2 x 2 x 2 = 32 pi / 3 cm cube. Step 3: Number of spheres = 288 pi / (32 pi / 3) = 288 x 3 / 32 = 27. Shortcut: pi cancels, so the count is (6 x 6 x 8 x 3) / (4 x 8) = 27. Trap (C): Using the cone formula (1/3 pi r squared h) for the cylinder gives 96 pi, and 96 pi / (32 pi / 3) = 9. Trap (A): Using (4/3) pi r squared (square instead of cube) for the sphere gives 16 pi / 3, and 288 pi / (16 pi / 3) = 54. Trap (B): Using the diameter 12 as the radius gives a cylinder volume of pi x 12 x 12 x 8 = 1152 pi, and 1152 pi / (32 pi / 3) = 108.

questions.question_text: The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 60 years. Five years ago, the father was 4 times as old as the son was at that time. What is the present age of the son?
questions.trap_type: Applying the age condition to present ages or reporting the wrong age
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Let the son's present age be S, so the father's age is 60 - S. Step 2: Five years ago: (60 - S - 5) = 4 x (S - 5), which gives 55 - S = 4S - 20. Step 3: 75 = 5S, so S = 15 years (father is 45). Check: five years ago father was 40 and son was 10, and 40 = 4 x 10. Shortcut: sum of ages five years ago = 60 - 10 = 50, split in the ratio 4 : 1 gives 40 and 10, so the son is 10 + 5 = 15 now. Trap (D): Applying the 4 : 1 condition to present ages gives 60 / 5 = 12 for the son. Trap (C): Reporting the son's age five years ago instead of now gives 10. Trap (A): Using +5 instead of -5 (as if the condition were five years later) gives 60 - S + 5 = 4 x (S + 5), so 45 = 5S and S = 9.

questions.question_text: The monthly electricity consumption of a government office decreases by 20% after energy-saving measures are introduced. In the following month, consumption increases by 12.5% because of additional equipment. If the original monthly consumption was 2400 units, what is the final consumption?
questions.trap_type: Adding successive percentage changes
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: After a 20% decrease, consumption is 2400 × 0.80 = 1920. Step 2: Increase 1920 by 12.5%: 1920 × 1.125 = 2160. Shortcut: 2400 × 80/100 × 112.5/100 = 2160. Trap (A): Applying both percentages to the original base gives 2400 − 480 + 300 = 2220. Trap (D): Applying the 12.5% decrease to 1920 instead of an increase gives 1920 × 0.875 = 1680. Trap (B): Applying the 20% decrease twice gives 2400 × 0.8 × 0.8 = 1536.

questions.question_text: A shopkeeper marks a water purifier 40% above its cost price and offers a discount of 15% on the marked price. If the selling price is Rs. 3570, what is the cost price?
questions.trap_type: Applying discount to cost price
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Let cost price be x. Marked price = 1.40x; selling price = 1.40x × 0.85 = 1.19x. Thus x = 3570/1.19 = 3000. Shortcut: CP = SP × 100/(140 × 85/100) = 3000. Trap (D): Treating the 15% discount as 15% of cost price gives SP = 1.40x − 0.15x = 1.25x, so x = 3570/1.25 = 2856; this does not match B, so B is not a valid trap. Trap (A): Assuming the selling price is 127.5% of cost price gives 3570/1.275 = 2800, which combines the markup and discount incorrectly. Trap (C): Using a 10% net profit gives 3570/1.10 ≈ 3245.45, not D. Distractors should be recalibrated before use.

questions.question_text: A laboratory has two salt solutions containing 30% and 50% salt, respectively. In what ratio should the first solution be mixed with the second to obtain a solution containing 42% salt?
questions.trap_type: Reversing the alligation ratio
questions.pedagogical_explanation: By alligation, the ratio of the 30% solution to the 50% solution is (50 − 42):(42 − 30) = 8:12 = 2:3. Shortcut: Cross-differences give the required ratio directly. Trap (D): Reversing the ratio gives 3:2. Trap (A): Using 50 − 42 and 50 − 30 gives 8:20 = 2:5, not C, so C is not a valid trap. Trap (C): Swapping the cross-differences also gives 3:2, duplicating B. Options A and C should be replaced in a production question bank.

questions.question_text: A and B invest Rs. 48,000 and Rs. 60,000, respectively, in a business. After 4 months, A withdraws half of his investment. B keeps his investment unchanged for the entire year. If the annual profit is Rs. 46,000, what is A's share of the profit?
questions.trap_type: Ignoring the duration of investment
questions.pedagogical_explanation: A's capital-time = 48000 × 4 + 24000 × 8 = 384000. B's capital-time = 60000 × 12 = 720000. Profit ratio = 384000:720000 = 8:15. A's share = 46000 × 8/23 = Rs. 16000. Shortcut: Compare capital × months, then divide the profit in that ratio. Trap (D): Using a 7:16 profit ratio gives 46000 × 7/23 = 14000, reflecting an incorrect capital-time total. Trap (A): Using a 9:14 ratio gives 46000 × 9/23 = 18000, reflecting an incorrect duration adjustment. Trap (C): Treating A's capital as unchanged for the full year gives ratio 48000:60000 = 4:5 and share 46000 × 4/9 ≈ 20444.44, not exactly Rs. 20000; this is not a valid exact trap.

questions.question_text: A sum of Rs. 20,000 is invested at 10% per annum, compounded annually. What is the compound interest earned at the end of 2 years?
questions.trap_type: Using simple interest instead of compound interest
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Amount after 2 years = 20000 × 1.10 × 1.10 = 24200. Compound interest = 24200 − 20000 = Rs. 4200. Shortcut: For 2 years, CI = P × (2r/100 + r²/10000) = 20000 × 0.21 = 4200. Trap (B): Simple interest gives 20000 × 10 × 2/100 = 4000. Trap (C): Adding only half of the second year's interest gives 4000 + 100 = 4100. Trap (A): Using a 10% rate for the first year and 12% for the second gives 20000 × 1.10 × 1.12 − 20000 = 4640, so D is not a valid trap and should be replaced in a production bank.

questions.question_text: Pipe A can fill a water tank in 12 hours, while pipe B can fill it in 18 hours. A leak at the bottom can empty the full tank in 36 hours. If all three are opened together, how long will it take to fill the empty tank?
questions.trap_type: Ignoring the leak
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Net rate = 1/12 + 1/18 − 1/36 = 3/36 + 2/36 − 1/36 = 4/36 = 1/9 tank per hour. Time = 9 hours. Shortcut: With LCM 36, the net rate is 3 + 2 − 1 = 4 units/hour, so time = 36/4 = 9 hours. Trap (D): Treating the leak as an additional filling pipe gives rate 3/36 + 2/36 + 1/36 = 6/36 and time 6 hours. Trap (C): Ignoring the leak gives rate 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36 and time 36/5 = 7.2 hours, not 8; B is not a valid trap. Trap (B): Ignoring pipe B gives net rate 1/12 − 1/36 = 2/36 and time 18 hours, not 12. Option C and B are not valid distractors and should be replaced.

questions.question_text: A train 180 metres long crosses a pole in 12 seconds. At the same speed, how long will it take to cross a platform 270 metres long?
questions.trap_type: Using only the platform length
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Speed = 180/12 = 15 m/s. To cross the platform, the train covers 180 + 270 = 450 metres. Time = 450/15 = 30 seconds. Shortcut: Add the train and platform lengths, then divide by speed. Trap (A): Using only the platform length gives 270/15 = 18 seconds. Trap (C): Using only the train length plus half the platform length gives (180 + 180)/15 = 24 seconds, an unsupported partial-distance error. Trap (B): Doubling the correct distance gives 900/15 = 60 seconds, so D is not a valid trap. Replace B and D before production use.

questions.question_text: The average score of 8 candidates in a recruitment test is 64. When the score of one candidate is removed, the average of the remaining 7 candidates becomes 61. What was the score of the candidate removed?
questions.trap_type: Subtracting averages instead of totals
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Total score of 8 candidates = 8 × 64 = 512. Total of the remaining 7 = 7 × 61 = 427. Removed score = 512 − 427 = 85. Shortcut: Removed score = n × old average − (n − 1) × new average. Trap (B): Subtracting the averages and adding the difference to the new average gives 61 + (64 − 61) = 64, not 80, so B is not a valid trap. Trap (D): Using 8 × (64 − 61) = 24 confuses average change with the removed score. Trap (C): Using 8 × 64 − 7 × 60 gives 92, not 88; D is not a valid trap.

questions.question_text: A rectangular training hall is 24 metres long and 18 metres wide. A uniform 2-metre-wide walkway is constructed inside the hall along all four walls. What is the area of the remaining central floor?
questions.trap_type: Subtracting the walkway width only once
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Central length = 24 − 2 × 2 = 20 metres. Central width = 18 − 2 × 2 = 14 metres. Remaining area = 20 × 14 = 280 square metres. Shortcut: Subtract twice the walkway width from both dimensions before multiplying. Trap (B): Using 20 × 16 = 320 subtracts the walkway width twice from the length but only once from the width. Trap (A): Using the full length and reduced width gives 24 × 14 = 336. Trap (C): Subtracting the walkway width only once from both dimensions gives 22 × 16 = 352.

questions.question_text: The population of a town increased by 10% in the first year and then decreased by 10% in the second year. If the population at the end of two years is 19,800, what was the population at the start of the first year?
questions.trap_type: Net percentage change miscalculation
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Let the initial population be P. After year 1 it becomes P x 1.1. After year 2 it becomes P x 1.1 x 0.9 = 0.99P. Step 2: 0.99P = 19800, so P = 19800/0.99 = 20000. Shortcut: net% change for successive +10% and -10% = 10 - 10 - (10x10)/100 = -1%, so final = 0.99 x initial. Trap (B) 19800: assumed +10% and -10% cancel out completely, so thought there was no net change and the starting population equals the final one. Trap (A) 24750: treated the two changes as a straight 20% decrease (10+10), ignoring that one change was an increase: P x 0.8 = 19800, giving P = 24750. Trap (C) 18000: forgot to apply the second year's decrease and used only the first year's 10% increase: P x 1.1 = 19800, giving P = 18000.

questions.question_text: A trader marks his goods 40% above the cost price and then allows a discount of 25% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?
questions.trap_type: Additive percentage trap / markup-discount confusion
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Let CP = 100. Marked price = 100 x 1.4 = 140. Step 2: Selling price after 25% discount = 140 x 0.75 = 105. Step 3: Profit = 105 - 100 = 5, so profit percent = 5%. Shortcut: net% = x + y + xy/100 with x = +40 (markup) and y = -25 (discount) = 40 - 25 - (40x25)/100 = 15 - 10 = 5%. Trap (A) 40%: forgot to apply the discount at all and mistook the markup percentage itself for the profit percentage. Trap (D) 15%: simply subtracted the two percentages (40 - 25 = 15) without accounting for the compounding effect between markup and discount. Trap (B) 25%: confused the discount percentage with the profit percentage and directly reported the discount value as the profit.
questions.verify_code:
cp = 100.0
mp = cp*1.4
sp = mp*0.75
answer = sp - cp

questions.question_text: A shopkeeper mixes two varieties of tea costing Rs. 20 per kg and Rs. 80 per kg. In what ratio must he mix them so that the resulting mixture costs Rs. 35 per kg? (Give the ratio of cheaper : dearer)
questions.trap_type: Alligation ratio inversion
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: By the rule of alligation, ratio (cheaper : dearer) = (Dearer price - Mean price) : (Mean price - Cheaper price). Step 2: = (80 - 35) : (35 - 20) = 45 : 15 = 3 : 1. Trap (C) 1:3: swapped the two differences, writing (Mean - Cheaper) : (Dearer - Mean) = 15 : 45 = 1 : 3, reversing which difference belongs to which variety. Trap (D) 4:1: used the full price gap (Dearer - Cheaper) in the numerator instead of (Dearer - Mean): (80 - 20) : (35 - 20) = 60 : 15 = 4 : 1. Trap (B) 3:4: kept (Dearer - Mean) correctly in the numerator but used the full price gap (Dearer - Cheaper) in the denominator instead of (Mean - Cheaper): (80 - 35) : (80 - 20) = 45 : 60 = 3 : 4.

questions.question_text: A and B started a business with investments of Rs. 45,000 and Rs. 60,000 respectively. After 6 months, A increased his investment by Rs. 15,000, while B's investment remained unchanged throughout the year. Find the ratio of their profits at the end of the year (A:B).
questions.trap_type: Time-weighting error in partnership
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: A's capital-months = 45000 x 6 (first half) + 60000 x 6 (second half, after the increase) = 270000 + 360000 = 630000. Step 2: B's capital-months = 60000 x 12 = 720000. Step 3: Ratio A:B = 630000 : 720000 = 7 : 8 (dividing both by 90000). Trap (D) 1:1: used only the final investment amounts (A becomes 60000 after the increase, same as B's 60000) without weighting by time at all, wrongly getting equal shares. Trap (A) 3:4: used only the original investment amounts, 45000:60000 = 3:4, completely ignoring the mid-year increase in A's investment. Trap (B) 11:8: applied A's increased investment (60000) for the full 12 months instead of only the remaining 6 months: A's capital-months = 45000x6 + 60000x12 = 990000, giving 990000:720000 = 11:8.

questions.question_text: Find the compound interest on Rs. 25,000 for 2 years at 8% per annum, compounded annually.
questions.trap_type: Simple interest vs compound interest confusion
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Amount = 25000 x 1.08 x 1.08 = 25000 x 1.1664 = 29160. Step 2: Compound interest = Amount - Principal = 29160 - 25000 = 4160. Trap (A) Rs. 2000: calculated interest for only the first year (25000 x 8% = 2000) and forgot to account for the second year's interest entirely. Trap (D) Rs. 29160: correctly calculated the total amount after 2 years but forgot to subtract the principal to isolate the compound interest. Trap (C) Rs. 4000: used the simple interest formula instead of compound interest: SI = (25000 x 8 x 2)/100 = 4000.

questions.question_text: Pipe A can fill a tank in 10 hours and pipe B can fill it in 15 hours, while pipe C (an outlet) can empty the full tank in 12 hours. If all three pipes are opened together, in how many hours will the tank be filled?
questions.trap_type: Sign/inclusion error with outlet pipe
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Take the tank capacity as the LCM of 10, 15, 12 = 60 units. Step 2: A fills 6 units/hr, B fills 4 units/hr, C empties 5 units/hr. Step 3: Net rate (all open together) = 6 + 4 - 5 = 5 units/hr. Step 4: Time = 60/5 = 12 hours. Trap (D) 4 hours: treated the outlet pipe C as another inlet pipe, adding its rate instead of subtracting it: net rate = 6+4+5 = 15 units/hr, time = 60/15 = 4 hours. Trap (C) 6 hours: ignored pipe C entirely and used only pipes A and B: net rate = 6+4 = 10 units/hr, time = 60/10 = 6 hours. Trap (A) 60 hours: ignored pipe B entirely and used only pipes A and C: net rate = 6-5 = 1 unit/hr, time = 60/1 = 60 hours.
questions.verify_code:
tank = 60
a = tank/10
b = tank/15
c = tank/12
net = a+b-c
answer = tank/net

questions.question_text: A train 150 m long crosses a platform 250 m long in 20 seconds. Find the speed of the train in km/h.
questions.trap_type: Incomplete distance / unit conversion error
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Total distance covered while crossing the platform = length of train + length of platform = 150 + 250 = 400 m. Step 2: Speed = 400/20 = 20 m/s. Step 3: Convert to km/h: 20 x 18/5 = 72 km/h. Trap (B) 27 km/h: used only the train's own length and ignored the platform: 150/20 = 7.5 m/s = 27 km/h. Trap (C) 20 km/h: correctly found the speed as 20 m/s but forgot to convert it into km/h before reporting it. Trap (D) 45 km/h: used only the platform's length and ignored the train's own length: 250/20 = 12.5 m/s = 45 km/h.
questions.verify_code:
distance = 150+250
time = 20
speed_mps = distance/time
answer = speed_mps*18/5

questions.question_text: A boat covers 36 km downstream in 2 hours and covers the same distance upstream in 3 hours. Find the speed of the boat in still water (in km/h).
questions.trap_type: Still-water vs stream speed confusion
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Downstream speed = 36/2 = 18 km/h. Step 2: Upstream speed = 36/3 = 12 km/h. Step 3: Speed of boat in still water = (downstream + upstream)/2 = (18+12)/2 = 15 km/h. Trap (B) 18 km/h: reported the downstream speed itself as the still-water speed, forgetting to average it with the upstream speed. Trap (A) 12 km/h: reported the upstream speed itself as the still-water speed, forgetting to average it with the downstream speed. Trap (D) 3 km/h: calculated the speed of the stream, (18-12)/2 = 3, instead of the speed of the boat, mixing up the two related formulas.

questions.question_text: The average weight of 8 boys in a class is 52 kg. When a 9th boy joins the group, the average weight becomes 54 kg. Find the weight of the new boy.
questions.trap_type: Average-addition formula misapplication
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Total weight of the original 8 boys = 8 x 52 = 416 kg. Step 2: Total weight of all 9 boys = 9 x 54 = 486 kg. Step 3: Weight of the new boy = 486 - 416 = 70 kg. Trap (C) 16 kg: computed the new total weight using the old number of boys (8) instead of the new number (9): 8 x 54 = 432, then 432 - 416 = 16. Trap (B) 54 kg: assumed the new boy's weight simply equals the new average weight, without doing the actual total-weight calculation. Trap (A) 18 kg: misapplied the shortcut formula by using (new average - old average) x new count of boys instead of old count: (54-52) x 9 = 18.

questions.question_text: The length of a rectangular field is 4 m more than its breadth. If the perimeter of the field is 64 m, find its area.
questions.trap_type: Perimeter formula algebra error
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step 1: Let breadth = b, so length = b + 4. Step 2: Perimeter = 2(l+b) = 2(2b+4) = 4b + 8 = 64, so 4b = 56 and b = 14, giving l = 18. Step 3: Area = 14 x 18 = 252 sq.m. Trap (A) 1020 sq.m: forgot the factor of 2 in the perimeter formula and used l+b = 64 directly: b+4+b=64, 2b=60, b=30, l=34, Area=30x34=1020. Trap (B) 320 sq.m: made an algebra slip while isolating b, using 4b = 64 instead of 4b = 64-8: b=16, l=20, Area=16x20=320. Trap (C) 64 sq.m: carelessly reported the given perimeter value itself as the final answer instead of calculating the area.

questions.question_text: The market value of an industrial machine increases by 20% in the first year, increases by 25% in the second year, and then depreciates by 10% in the third year. If its value at the end of the third year is Rs. 54,000, what was its original value at the beginning of the first year?
questions.trap_type: Reversing the percentages on the final value or undoing only one of the three changes
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step-by-step: Let the original value be P. The three changes act multiplicatively: P × (120/100) × (125/100) × (90/100) = 54,000, i.e. P × (6/5) × (5/4) × (9/10) = P × 27/20 = 54,000, so P = 54,000 × 20/27 = Rs. 40,000. Shortcut: combined multiplier = 1.2 × 1.25 × 0.9 = 1.35; original value = 54,000 ÷ 1.35 = Rs. 40,000. Trap (C): 'Reversing' each change on the final value by subtracting 20%, subtracting 25% and adding 10% (54,000 × 0.8 × 0.75 × 1.1 = Rs. 35,640) instead of dividing by the multipliers. Trap (D): Undoing only the 10% depreciation (54,000 ÷ 0.9 = Rs. 60,000) and forgetting the two increases. Trap (A): Treating the 10% depreciation as a 10% appreciation (multiplier 1.2 × 1.25 × 1.1 = 1.65), giving 54,000 ÷ 1.65 ≈ Rs. 32,727.

questions.concept_tag: Marked Price, Discount, and Profit Ratio
questions.question_text: A dealer marks an air purifier 40% above its cost price and allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. If he earns a net profit of Rs. 760 on the sale of one unit, what is the marked price of the air purifier?
questions.trap_type: Stopping at the Cost Price or subtracting discount % directly from markup %
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step-by-step: Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100x. Then the Marked Price (MP) is 140x. After a 15% discount on MP, the Selling Price (SP) is 140x × (85/100) = 119x. The net profit is SP - CP = 119x - 100x = 19x. Given 19x = Rs. 760, we get x = 40. Therefore, Marked Price = 140x = 140 × 40 = Rs. 5,600. Shortcut: Net profit % = 40 - 15 - (40 × 15)/100 = 19%. Since 19% of CP = 760, 1% of CP = 40, and MP (140% of CP) = 140 × 40 = Rs. 5,600. Trap (C): Stopping at the Cost Price (100x = 100 × 40 = Rs. 4,000) instead of finding the Marked Price. Trap (D): Subtracting the 15% discount linearly from the 40% markup (40% - 15% = 25% profit), which gives CP = 760 / 0.25 = Rs. 3,040 and MP = 3,040 × 1.4 = Rs. 4,256. Trap (B): Calculating the Selling Price (119x = 119 × 40 = Rs. 4,760) instead of the Marked Price.

questions.concept_tag: Dishonest Dealer with Markup and Faulty Weight
questions.question_text: A spice merchant marks his goods 20% above the cost price, offers a 10% discount to customers, and also uses a faulty weight of 900 grams instead of 1 kilogram. What is his actual overall profit percentage?
questions.trap_type: Dividing the weight gain by 1000g instead of 900g or ignoring the faulty weight
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step-by-step: Let the cost of 1 gram be Re. 1. For a nominal 1 kg the merchant marks Rs. 1,200 (+20%) and, after the 10% discount, the customer pays SP = 1,200 × 0.90 = Rs. 1,080. But he hands over only 900 g, which cost him Rs. 900. Profit = 1,080 − 900 = Rs. 180, so profit % = 180/900 × 100 = 20%. Shortcut: overall multiplier = (120/100) × (90/100) × (1000/900) = (6/5) × (9/10) × (10/9) = 6/5 = 1.20, i.e. 20% profit. Trap (A): Ignoring the faulty weight and taking only the markup-discount effect: 20 − 10 − (20 × 10)/100 = 8%. Trap (D): Dividing the Rs. 180 profit by the nominal 1,000 g instead of the actual 900 g cost: 180/1000 × 100 = 18%. Trap (B): Treating the 100 g shortfall as a 10% gain (100/1000 instead of 100/900) and compounding it with 8%: 8 + 10 + (8 × 10)/100 = 18.8%.

questions.question_text: A vessel contains 72 liters of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 5 : 4. If 18 liters of this mixture is taken out and replaced with 18 liters of pure water, what is the new ratio of milk to water in the vessel?
questions.trap_type: Adding the water without first removing mixture, taking all 18 litres from milk, or inverting the ratio
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step-by-step: Initially milk = 72 × 5/9 = 40 L and water = 72 × 4/9 = 32 L. Removing 18 L of mixture leaves 54 L in the same 5 : 4 ratio: milk = 54 × 5/9 = 30 L, water = 54 × 4/9 = 24 L. Adding 18 L of water gives water = 24 + 18 = 42 L. New ratio milk : water = 30 : 42 = 5 : 7. Shortcut: 18/72 = 1/4 of the mixture is replaced, so milk = (3/4) × 40 = 30 L and water = 72 − 30 = 42 L, giving 5 : 7. Trap (D): Adding the 18 L of water without first removing any mixture: 40 : (32 + 18) = 40 : 50 = 4 : 5. Trap (A): Reporting water : milk (42 : 30 = 7 : 5) instead of milk : water. Trap (B): Taking all 18 L out of the milk only and then adding 18 L of water: (40 − 18) : (32 + 18) = 22 : 50 = 11 : 25.

questions.question_text: A and B enter into a business partnership by investing Rs. 45,000 and Rs. 60,000 respectively. After 4 months, A invests an additional Rs. 15,000, while B withdraws Rs. 15,000. At the end of the year, if the total profit is Rs. 63,000, what is A's share of the profit?
questions.trap_type: Ignoring time weighting (using only initial or only final capitals) or finding B's share
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step-by-step: Work in units of Rs. 15,000. A has 3 units for the first 4 months and 3 + 1 = 4 units for the remaining 8 months: 3 × 4 + 4 × 8 = 12 + 32 = 44. B has 4 units for 4 months and 4 − 1 = 3 units for 8 months: 4 × 4 + 3 × 8 = 16 + 24 = 40. Profit ratio A : B = 44 : 40 = 11 : 10, so A's share = 11/21 × 63,000 = Rs. 33,000. Trap (B): Using only the capitals after the change (4 : 3), giving A = 4/7 × 63,000 = Rs. 36,000. Trap (A): Using only the initial capitals (45,000 : 60,000 = 3 : 4), giving A = 3/7 × 63,000 = Rs. 27,000. Trap (C): Computing B's share (10/21 × 63,000 = Rs. 30,000) instead of A's.

questions.question_text: If the difference between the compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal at 10% per annum for 3 years is Rs. 465, what is the principal amount?
questions.trap_type: Using the 2-year difference formula P(R/100)^2 or omitting the +R/100 term
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step-by-step: For 3 years at 10% p.a., Simple Interest = 3 * 10% = 30% of Principal (P), while Compound Interest = [(1.10)^3 - 1] * 100% = (1.331 - 1) * 100% = 33.1% of P. The difference is 33.1% - 30% = 3.1% of P. Given 3.1% of P = Rs. 465 => (3.1 / 100) * P = 465 => P = 46,500 / 3.1 = Rs. 15,000. Shortcut: 3-year CI - SI difference = P * (R/100)^2 * (3 + R/100) = P * (1/100) * (3.1) = 465 => P = Rs. 15,000. Trap (D): Using the 2-year difference formula P * (R/100)^2 = 465 => P * (1/100) = 465 => Rs. 46,500. Trap (A): Multiplying the 2-year difference by 3 instead of 3.1 (using 3% of P = 465) gives 46,500 / 3 = Rs. 15,500. Trap (B): Writing 3.1% as 0.31 instead of 0.031 (a decimal slip), which gives 465 / 0.31 = Rs. 1,500.

questions.question_text: What is the compound interest on a sum of Rs. 16,000 at 20% per annum for 1.5 years, when the interest is compounded half-yearly?
questions.trap_type: Using Simple Interest or forgetting to halve the annual rate for half-yearly periods
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step-by-step: Since interest is compounded half-yearly, the rate per half-year is R = 20% / 2 = 10%, and the number of half-year periods in 1.5 years is n = 1.5 * 2 = 3. Amount = 16,000 * (1 + 10/100)^3 = 16,000 * (11/10)^3 = 16 * 1331 = Rs. 21,296. Compound Interest = 21,296 - 16,000 = Rs. 5,296. Shortcut: For 3 periods at 10%, effective CI rate is 33.1%. 33.1% of 16,000 = 160 * 33.1 = Rs. 5,296. Trap (B): Calculating Simple Interest instead of Compound Interest (16,000 * 20% * 1.5 = Rs. 4,800). Trap (A): Compounding annually for 1 year at 20% and then taking 10% for the remaining half-year: 16,000 * 1.20 * 1.10 - 16,000 = 21,120 - 16,000 = Rs. 5,120. Trap (D): Halving the rate to 10% but using only 2 periods instead of 3 (21% of 16,000 = Rs. 3,360).

questions.concept_tag: Time and Work with Worker Leaving Early
questions.question_text: A and B can complete a project in 18 days and 24 days respectively. They begin working together, but A leaves 3 days before the completion of the project. For how many total days did the project last?
questions.trap_type: Reporting the days A and B worked together instead of total project days
questions.pedagogical_explanation: Step-by-step: Let total work = LCM(18, 24) = 72 units. Efficiency of A = 72 / 18 = 4 units/day; Efficiency of B = 72 / 24 = 3 units/day. In the last 3 days, B works alone and completes 3 * 3 = 9 units. The remaining 72 - 9 = 63 units were completed by A and B working together at 4 + 3 = 7 units/day, which took 63 / 7 = 9 days. Therefore, total duration of the project = 9 + 3 = 12 days. Shortcut: Add A's 3 days of unperformed work (3 * 4 = 12 units) to total work and divide by combined efficiency: (72 + 12) / (4 + 3) = 84 / 7 = 12 days. Trap (B): Stopping at the 9 days that A and B worked together and forgetting to add the final 3 days.
